rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source-of-income protection in housing
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone because of the lawful source of their income or of their rent payment, for example a Section 8 voucher. Complaints can be filed with the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days, or in Superior Court within two years.
rules.key_value: ban on source-of-income (incl. Section 8 voucher) discrimination
rules.quoted_span: This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
rules.effective_date_note: The brochure does not state when the source-of-income protection took effect.

unverifiable_exemptions: single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit
room rental in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling
religious organization preference for members of the same religion

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, business or residential.
rules.exemptions: Rental of one apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rental of rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious organization preference for people of the same religion.
rules.penalty: Complaint to the Division on Civil Rights (within 180 days) or NJ Superior Court (within two years).

parsed.doc_summary: NJ Division on Civil Rights brochure on the Law Against Discrimination in housing. The only in-scope rule is the source-of-income (Section 8 voucher) protection, which falls under screening restrictions. The brochure says nothing on the other categories.
